symptom: describe printed a decision whose true branch is empty as `if not(X) then <false branch> end if;`; executing the description stored not(X) with the true/false outcomes swapped — behaviour unchanged, model changed, so describe -> exec was not a round trip (mendixlabs/mxcli#1742)
cause: an 'empty-then swap' in traverseFlow / traverseFlowUntilMerge folded the decision for readability; #1930 then had to undo the fold in the condition-edit splice (decisionPrintedNegated), and alter targets carried the stored form as an Alternate
file: mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_show_helpers.go (swap removed, negateIfCondition / negateExpression / decisionPrintedNegated deleted), mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow.go (no fold to undo); tests flow_splice_negated_condition_pedapp_test.go (TestDescribeExec_EmptyThenDecisionRoundTrips), cmd_microflows_traverse_test.go, cmd_microflows_handles_test.go
insight: A describe that prints a NORMALISED form instead of the stored one is a standing round-trip defect: every consumer of the text inherits a compensation (the splice's un-negation, the handles' alternates), and each new consumer is a new place to forget one. Prefer printing what is stored when the grammar can express it — `if X then else … end if;` always parsed and builds exactly Studio Pro's shape. A script written against the old folded output still means the same thing: the splice diffs the branches independently, so `if not(Y) then B` over the stored `if X then else B` sets the condition and moves B, it does not invert. Its alter TARGETS in the folded form no longer resolve — a refusal, never a wrong edit. Control: with the fold restored, the PedApp round-trip test reproduces the reporter's table exactly (not($Sale/Code != empty), outcomes swapped).
